title: Testing new support for people with multiple long-term health conditions
official: CO-ACTION: Personalised social and self-management support for better living with multiple long-term conditions in the community
summary:
Background and study aims 
The prevalence of multiple long-term conditions/multimorbidity (MLTC-M) is rising. Current care primarily focuses on individual conditions, acute symptoms, and medication reviews ,neglecting broader needs like mobility, functioning, social isolation, mental health, and wellbeing, leading to fragmentation of care. Access to joined up health, social care and voluntary support services is limited. This results in a high incidence of unplanned hospital admissions, lack of personalised attention and higher costs. This trial will compare the CO-ACTION intervention to usual care. Around 300 participants (plus additional informal carers) will help assess the CO-ACTION intervention looking at wellbeing, quality of life and unplanned hospitalisations alongside a cost-effectiveness evaluation.  

Who can participate?
Adults with 2 or more long-term conditions, indication of biopsychosocial need or no engagement with healthcare services in the last 12 months with self-reported need for an intervention. 

What does the study involve?
Participants will have a screening call with a researcher and if eligible a baseline data collection visit (including consent and randomisation to determine which study group a participant will take part in). There will be follow-up data collection visits after 3-months, 6-month and 12-months. Participants in the intervention group will have at least three sessions with the CO-ACTION facilitator where needs will be prioritised and a support plan created and agreed. Informal carers may be recruited alongside participant with multiple long-term conditions. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Benefits: Contributing to the development of new knowledge and understanding, which could help improve MLTC-M management in the future.
Risks: No considerable risks have been identified. 

Where is the study run from?
Peninsula Clinical Trials Unit (PenCTU), University of Plymouth, UK.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
October 2026 to September 2028.

Who is funding the study?
National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), UK.

Who is the main contact?
Katherine Beaney, coaction.penctu@plymouth.ac.uk.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Have a confirmed diagnosis* of two or more of high impact long-term non-communicable conditions from this list:  
1.1.	Arthritis or problem with back or joints
1.2.	Autism or autism spectrum condition
1.3.	Blindness or partial sight
1.4.	Cancer in the last five years
1.5.	Deafness or hearing loss
1.6.	Dementia or Alzheimer’s disease
1.7.	Diabetes
1.8.	Frailty
1.9.	Heart or Cardiovascular condition
1.10.	High blood pressure
1.11.	Kidney or liver disease
1.12.	Learning disability
1.13.	Lung or breathing condition
1.14.	Mental Health condition
1.15.	Neurological condition
1.16.	Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA)
2.	Have EITHER a confirmed indication of biopsychosocial need OR no (healthcare) service use in the 12 months plus a self-reported need for an intervention
3.	Not be currently receiving an intervention or service similar to the CO-ACTION intervention  
4.	Aged 18 years or over
5.	Have capacity to and be willing to provide informed consent 
*Self-reported for those not recruited from healthcare settings.
Exclusion criteria:
Not meeting the key inclusion criteria
